binding_note: 1 TB counted as in plus out is 0.6 TB each way, which at 3.24 Mbit/s sustained is about 34 days of the 1 TiB/month target, and the count is bidirectional so the usable one-way figure is half the headline. The 100 Mbps rate is 32.4 TB/day, so the quota binds long before the rate.

reliability_note: exceeding the quota does not cut the tunnel, it shapes it to 64-256 kbps, which keeps SSH and SMTP alive and makes bulk transfer impractical
confidence_note: A transfer through a provisioned interface would raise this to measured and would confirm that inbound ports really are open.

notes: The only provider in this lane where a standard .conf plus a real public IPv4 plus no port blocking was all stated first-party. It fails the free test, not the technical one: at USD 8/mo for 1 TB it is the cheapest documented route to a public address that carries UDP. metered_on is recorded as unstated because the vocabulary has no token for a bidirectional sum; the vendor sentence is in volume_stated. Merged from the duplicate record `hoppy-network`: Not free, and included because it is the cleanest statement in this lane that a WireGuard tunnel can carry a public IPv4 with no port blocking, and because the over-limit behaviour is unusual: the interface is throttled rather than cut, so inbound stays alive at 64 to 256 kbps. At 256 kbps that is 2.76 GB/day, which is 0.08 TiB/month: unusable for the stated workload and enough for SSH. Yggdrasil traffic on the private relay is not counted toward the cap.
